# relgap audit

Scans each root for repositories the way 'relgap drift' does and asks OSV about the version
of every pin: one query per tool, version and OSV package, however many repositories pin it.
--tool limits the run to the named tools. Ignore rules in the config drop matching pins.

An exact pin is checked at its own version and needs no lookup for it. A value marked ≈ is
checked at the version it stands for, the CURRENT of 'relgap outdated': a constraint (~&gt; 1.15)
takes the highest exact pin of the tool in the same repository that satisfies it, otherwise
the lowest version that does; a prefix (26) takes the highest stable version that starts with
it; the latest channel takes the latest version. To find the version, only these pins need
the tool's versions from GitHub or another host.

A pin with a curated osv list in its registry entry queries those packages. Other pins query
the package their backend names (npm:, pypi:, cargo:, gem:, go:, dotnet:), or the Go module
and git repository of a github.com tool. An action pin (scan.detectors.ci\_actions) queries the
GitHub Actions package of its repository once without a version, because OSV doesn't match
those ranges to a version, and relgap matches them itself. A pin by commit SHA is checked at
the version its line comment names (# v4.1.3), as Renovate reads it; without one it is
not-exact. A finding is one advisory that affects one tool
version, with every pin of that version, its severity, the lowest fixed version and its
osv.dev page. A record without a rating takes the rating of its GHSA alias, else its severity
is unknown. Findings sort by severity, unknown last, then by ID; with --kev and --epss,
findings in the KEV catalog come first and the EPSS score breaks ties of severity.

Each finding has a fix target, listed under "Fix targets" and as fix in --format json: the
lowest stable release above the version that every advisory with a fix has left behind, and
the same within the version's line. Candidates are checked against the advisories' ranges,
then OSV is asked about them and the latest release; a candidate with an advisory of its own
moves the target on. An advisory the latest release still has is one no release fixes (fix is
null), and relgap warns when the latest release has any. Only a tool version with findings
lists its tool's versions for this.

A pin OSV wasn't asked about is listed with the reason, and never counts as clean:
no-advisory-source, private-source, not-exact, unresolved, offline or failed.

Config vulns.ignore suppresses an advisory by its ID or any alias, with a required reason, an
optional until date and optional tools globs (kubectl, npm:\*, action:actions/\*). --vex
(config vulns.vex) reads OpenVEX v0.2.0 documents: the latest statement about an advisory
whose product or subcomponent purl names the pin suppresses it when it says not\_affected or
fixed. A suppressed advisory is listed under "Suppressed" with its reason (suppressed in
--format json), doesn't count for --fail-on and doesn't hold back the fix target. relgap
warns about an entry past its until date, which suppresses nothing, and, without --tool,
about an entry that suppressed nothing.

--kev (config vulns.kev) marks the findings whose CVE is in the CISA Known Exploited
Vulnerabilities catalog, which relgap fetches from www.cisa.gov once a day, with the date CISA
added it and whether it knows of ransomware use: a KEV column, and kev in --format json and
SARIF. --epss (config vulns.epss) adds each finding's FIRST EPSS score, the probability of
exploitation in the next 30 days, from api.first.org: an EPSS column with the percentile, and
epss in --format json and SARIF. Both are off by default. When a feed is down, relgap warns,
--format json lists the error, and the report goes on without that field.

--format openvex writes an OpenVEX v0.2.0 document: one statement per advisory and tool
version, affected with the fix target as the action statement, and not\_affected (or the VEX
status that suppressed it) with the reason. Products are the purls of the advisories'
packages, such as pkg:golang/stdlib@v1.22.0, pkg:npm/lodash@4.17.20 or
pkg:githubactions/actions/checkout@v4.1.2.

--format sarif writes a SARIF 2.1.0 log for GitHub code scanning: a result per finding at each
pin's file and line (one rule per OSV ID), a note per unchecked pin (unchecked), and a result
per file or version lookup that failed (failed). The results don't depend on --fail-on.

--fail-on takes vuln, unchecked and kev. vuln counts the findings at or above --vuln-severity
and those of unknown severity, and with --vuln-fixable only those with a fixed version above
the pinned one. unchecked counts the unchecked tool versions. kev counts the findings in the
KEV catalog, whatever their severity, and needs --kev. audit gates vuln by default. Values
in config policy.fail\_on that audit checks add to vuln, and --fail-on replaces the whole set:
--fail-on unchecked gates only unchecked, and --fail-on= gates nothing. A value whose count
reaches --min-count (default 1) exits 3. Otherwise a file or lookup that failed exits 1, and
so does an OSV outage under --fail-on vuln or a KEV outage under --fail-on kev, since a pass on
partial data proves nothing.

--offline answers from the HTTP cache. Pins without a cached answer are unchecked with reason
offline, and --format json has oldest\_answer, when the oldest OSV answer was stored.

Roots default to scan.roots, then the current directory.

## Usage

```sh
relgap audit [roots...] [flags]
```

## Arguments

| Argument | Required | Repeatable |
|---|---|---|
| `roots` | no | yes |

## Flags

| Flag | Description | Type | Default | Values | Config key | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--epss` | add each advisory's FIRST EPSS score, asking api.first.org about its CVE IDs (config vulns.epss) | bool |  |  | [`vulns.epss`](/reference/config#vulns-epss) |  |
| `--fail-on` | exit 3 when this matches: vuln, unchecked or kev; repeatable; replaces the default vuln, which config policy.fail\_on adds to | list, repeatable |  | `vuln`: a known vulnerability in a pinned version<br>`unchecked`: a pinned version OSV wasn't asked about<br>`kev`: a known vulnerability in the CISA KEV catalog; needs --kev | [`policy.fail_on`](/reference/config#policy-fail-on) |  |
| `--kev` | mark advisories in the CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, fetched from www.cisa.gov (config vulns.kev) | bool |  |  | [`vulns.kev`](/reference/config#vulns-kev) |  |
| `--md-max-chars` | cut Markdown output to this many characters at a row or section boundary; 0 means no limit | int | `60000` |  |  |  |
| `--min-count` | findings a --fail-on value needs before it exits 3 | int | `1` |  |  |  |
| `--out` | also write the report to a file as format=path (repeatable); format is one of plain, md, json, sarif, github or openvex | string, repeatable |  | `plain`: table without color<br>`md`: Markdown<br>`json`: JSON envelope for scripts<br>`sarif`: SARIF 2.1.0 for code scanning<br>`github`: GitHub Actions annotations<br>`openvex`: OpenVEX v0.2.0 document |  |  |
| `--submodules` | scan checked-out git submodules as repositories | bool |  |  |  |  |
| `--tool` | audit only this tool; repeatable | list, repeatable |  |  |  |  |
| `--vex` | OpenVEX v0.2.0 document whose not\_affected and fixed statements suppress advisories; repeatable; replaces config vulns.vex | list, repeatable |  |  | [`vulns.vex`](/reference/config#vulns-vex) |  |
| `--vuln-fixable` | --fail-on vuln counts only advisories with a fixed version above the pinned one (config policy.vuln\_fixable) | bool |  |  | [`policy.vuln_fixable`](/reference/config#policy-vuln-fixable) |  |
| `--vuln-severity` | lowest rating --fail-on vuln counts: low, medium, high or critical; an unknown rating always counts, and empty counts all (config policy.vuln\_severity) | string |  | `low`: CVSS 0.1 to 3.9<br>`medium`: CVSS 4.0 to 6.9<br>`high`: CVSS 7.0 to 8.9<br>`critical`: CVSS 9.0 to 10.0 | [`policy.vuln_severity`](/reference/config#policy-vuln-severity) |  |

The [global flags](/cli/global-flags) work with every command.

## Output formats

`--format` accepts `tty`, `plain`, `md`, `json`, `sarif`, `github`, `openvex`. Without it, the format is `tty` when stdout is a terminal and `plain` otherwise. Formats are described on the [global flags](/cli/global-flags) page.

## Fail-on values

`--fail-on` makes the command exit 3 when the report has a match:

| Value | Matches |
|---|---|
| `vuln` | a known vulnerability in a pinned version |
| `unchecked` | a pinned version OSV wasn't asked about |
| `kev` | a known vulnerability in the CISA KEV catalog; needs --kev |

## Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | The command finished. With --fail-on, nothing matched. |
| 1 | The command failed: a read, a write, a child process or a check failed. |
| 2 | Wrong usage: an unknown command or flag, a bad value or argument, an invalid config file, or a prompt with no terminal. |
| 3 | A --fail-on gate matched. The report is still written. |
| 4 | Credentials were missing or rejected for every source the command needed. |
| 130 | Interrupted by Ctrl-C (SIGINT) or a cancelled context. |

All codes are listed on the [exit codes](/reference/exit-codes) page.

## Examples

```sh
relgap audit
relgap audit ~/src/infra ~/src/apps --format md
relgap audit --tool terraform --tool node
relgap audit --vuln-severity high --format sarif > audit.sarif
relgap audit --fail-on vuln --fail-on unchecked
relgap audit --vuln-fixable --vuln-severity high
relgap audit --kev --epss --fail-on kev
relgap audit --vex vex/platform.json --format openvex > audit.vex.json
relgap audit --format json | jq '.data.findings[] | {tool, version, id}'
```
